title: Per-request quality SLIs and error-escrow ledger for region-safe rollouts
creator: Leah Kim
description:
Goal: Define and operationalize a per-request quality SLI (Request Quality Score) for model endpoints and a ledger-style error-escrow mechanism that allows safe multi-region rollouts, controlled borrowing/lending of error budget, and deterministic circuit-breaker triggers. This work ties SLI definition to model-specific behavior (e.g., hallucination signals, function-call success, generation quality), establishes how to compute and aggregate token- and request-level signals into a single quality score, and specifies the governance for escrowed error budgets used during canaries, migrations, and region failovers.

Why: Current SLO documents focus on latency and availability bands but do not capture degradations in generation quality that matter for downstream product correctness. Region rollouts and multi-variant migrations need a conservative mechanism to avoid cascading user-visible failures while enabling controlled traffic movement.

Outcomes:
- Canonical per-request SLI definition and computation procedure (for hosted/Dedicated/Private).
- Error-escrow ledger design with APIs: deposit, withdraw, transfer, borrow limits, auto-recall rules.
- Circuit-breaker mapping from escrow burn rates and request-quality deciles to enforced shedding policies.
- Monitoring dashboards and alerting playbooks; runbook for rollback and emergency remediation.
- Migration checklist for rollouts with cross-region escrow reconciliation.
acceptance_criteria: Definition doc published in Confluence: per-request Request Quality Score (RQS) spec
Instrumentation: request-level RQS emitted via x-request-metrics with <50ms compute overhead
Error-escrow ledger API implemented with RBAC and audit logs
End-to-end test demonstrating controlled region failover using escrow transfer without SLA violations
Dashboards: RQS heatmap per-route, escrow balance ledger, burn-rate forecast widget
implementation_plan: Design: finalize RQS feature set (latency penalty, generation-confidence, function-call success, hallucination signals)
Schema: event-level tags and metrics (no nested payloads; proto contract v1)
Backend: escrow ledger service (lightweight state machine) and reconciler for multi-region eventual consistency
Runtime: integrate RQS emission into serving runtime with opt-in flag per model/endpoint
Control plane: console UI for viewing and adjusting escrow transfers and borrowing policies
QA: synthetic and canary tests with scripted burn scenarios and chaos tests for region partitions
Rollout: start with non-critical internal routes, then beta customers, then platform-wide enforcement
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: RQS false positives could trigger unnecessary circuit breakers — Mitigation: threshold calibration via A/B on historical prompt sets and grace windows
Risk: Escrow ledger cross-region race conditions — Mitigation: design reconciler with idempotent transfers and compensating transactions
Risk: Increased metric ingestion costs — Mitigation: downsample low-variance traffic and aggregate at 1s buckets where possible
Risk: Customer confusion about borrowed error budget — Mitigation: per-tenant ledger views and explanatory UI with audit trail
monitoring_and_alerts: Primary alert: escrow burn rate > 3x baseline for 5m => page oncall SRE
Secondary alert: median RQS drop > 20% for SLA-critical routes => trigger canary rollback
Info alert: escrow transfer initiated between regions (> $threshold ops) => notify infra-admins
Dashboards: per-route RQS distribution, escrow balances, burn-rate forecast, corrective action timeline
migration_checklist: Backfill: compute baseline RQS on historical 30-day traffic for target regions
Set escrow deposit: initial deposit = 2x expected daily burn for candidate region
Canary: route 1% traffic and monitor RQS + burn-rate for 12 hours
Scale: progress to 10% with automated borrow policy enabled, watch for anomalous hallucination signals
Finalize: switch routing and reconcile ledgers; post-mortem within 48h if burn exceeds threshold
